code-design.note: Catches the real duplicate FormatComments compile break, gives full signatures, numbered call chains, an error table and explicit assumptions, but leaves --debug printing to stdout so --debug -o json can still corrupt JSON.

superpowers.note: Accurate on Get-only client, local -o flag and stdout debug output, and has a good statusUpdater test seam, but misses the broken build on main while requiring make check to pass, and its single writer conflicts with the stderr notice.

feature-dev.note: Catches the compile break (with the merge commit), the stdout debug issue and the duplicated custom-ID logic, compares three architecture options, and covers zero-status and race edge cases, with only a minor unused teamID parameter.

plain.note: Short and mostly accurate (cobra routing verified), but misses the compile break, has no testable seam for the command flow, ignores -o json and debug stdout, and has the thinnest failure-path design.

reason: Y and W were the only plans to find that main does not compile (duplicate DetailFormatter.FormatComments, confirmed by go vet), which would break their own make check step, while X and Z missed it. Y edged W by also fixing debug output on stdout, adding a zero-statuses guard and comparing architecture options so the layering decision is visible and challengeable; X and Z were thinner on failure paths and testability.
